project.name: ShopFlow
project.description: Acme Retail checkout platform — cart, payments, inventory reservation, and storefront. Production revenue path.

memories.title: ADR-0007: Stripe as primary payment processor
memories.body:
Decision: Use Stripe PaymentIntents as the primary payment processor for ShopFlow. PayPal remains a secondary fallback for regions where Stripe conversion is weak.

Context: We evaluated Stripe, Adyen, and Braintree. Stripe won on developer experience, webhook reliability, and existing Acme Retail billing relationships.

Consequences: All new payment code must go through services/payments/src/stripeAdapter.ts. Direct Stripe SDK usage in checkout is forbidden. Idempotency keys are mandatory on every charge.

memories.title: ADR-0012: Inventory reservation before payment auth
memories.body:
Decision: Reserve inventory when a checkout session is created, before payment authorization. Release reservations on payment failure or session expiry (15 minutes).

Context: In November 2024 we oversold limited drops because stock was only decremented after payment success. Marketing launched flash sales while checkout raced.

Consequences: checkout/session.ts must call inventory.reserve(). Never complete payment without an active reservation ID.

memories.title: INC-2141: Payment confirmation timeouts
memories.body:
Incident: On 2025-03-12, ~18% of checkouts failed with payment confirmation timeouts during a marketing campaign.

Root cause: chargeCustomer() was called without idempotency keys under retry storms from the mobile client. Stripe created duplicate PaymentIntents; our webhook handler could not reconcile sessions.

Fix: Require idempotencyKey on ChargeRequest. Checkout now derives the key from checkoutSessionId + attempt number. Added alerting on pending payment intents older than 2 minutes.

Lesson: Retries without idempotency in payments are a production outage waiting to happen.

memories.title: Why ShopFlow exists
memories.body:
ShopFlow is Acme Retail's unified checkout platform. It replaced three legacy checkout stacks (web monolith, iOS native, partner marketplace) so pricing, promotions, tax, and payments stay consistent.

Business problem: fragmented checkout caused cart abandonment and incorrect promotions. ShopFlow owns cart → checkout → payment → inventory reservation for web and mobile.

If you are onboarding: start with demo/shopflow/README.md, then read ADR-0007 and ADR-0012 before changing payments or inventory.

memories.title: Checkout session lifecycle
memories.body:
Feature: Checkout sessions move draft → awaiting_payment → paid | failed | cancelled.

createCheckoutSession reserves inventory and creates a payment intent via the payments adapter. completeCheckout is triggered by Stripe webhooks, not by the browser redirect alone.

Production impact: this path is on the critical revenue path for all Acme Retail digital orders.

memories.title: Cart service ownership boundary
memories.body:
The cart service owns mutable cart state only. It must not call Stripe or finalize orders. Checkout reads an immutable cart snapshot at session creation.

Refactor note (2025-01): promotions were moved out of cart into a separate promotions engine to stop double-discount bugs.

memories.title: Guest checkout must still reserve inventory
memories.body:
Product rule: guest users can checkout without an account, but inventory reservation rules are identical to logged-in users. Do not special-case guests in reserve().

This was clarified after support tickets where guest flash-sale purchases oversold SKUs.

memories.title: Webhook-driven payment completion
memories.body:
Design decision: Browser success redirects are UX only. Source of truth for paid status is the Stripe payment_intent.succeeded webhook processed by checkout.

Never mark a session paid solely from client-side confirmation — fraud and double-submit risk.

impact_links.user_segment: All web and mobile buyers paying by card
impact_links.notes: Breaking chargeCustomer() or idempotency behavior can halt revenue. See INC-2141.
Owns revenue-critical lifecycle. Inventory reservation must remain before payment auth.
Incorrect totals propagate into checkout payment amounts.
Module-level blast radius for any payment adapter change.
